description: pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:81 — `use std::{fs, io, vec::Vec};` imports `Vec` from `std::vec`. The workspace uses `edition = "2021"`, which includes `Vec` in the prelude. The explicit import is redundant noise. Fix: `use std::{fs, io};` (or split as `use std::fs;` / `use std::io;` if preferred). Confirmed no semantic change — `Vec` in the prelude resolves to the same `std::vec::Vec`. What goes wrong if it stays: extra import to skim past; mildly suggests the author either copy-pasted from a no_std crate or wasn't certain about the prelude (neither is true based on the rest of the diff, which uses no_std-flavored `core::fmt::*` imports — but `Vec` is a different layer).
title: use std::{fs, io, vec::Vec} imports Vec redundantly (already in 2021 prelude)
